paper.one_line_finding: Relative to Human-only, access to up to five GPT-4 story ideas raised evaluator-rated novelty by 8.1 percent (b = 0.311, P < 0.001) and usefulness by 9.0 percent (b = 0.453, P < 0.001) (p. 3, Fig. 2A), while stories in both AI arms were more similar to the other stories in their condition (one idea b = 0.871, P < 0.001; five ideas b = 0.718, P = 0.003) (p. 4; Fig. 4B, p. 5).

estimates.notes: The analysis is at the rating level. The paper specifies robust SEs clustered by evaluator, not by the randomized writer (PDF p. 8). se_basis is coded rating to flag that the uncertainty does not account for repeated ratings of each writer; regression.se_type, when present, is clustered_cluster for evaluator clusters. n_units is the printed total of evaluations across the full three-arm analysis, not a printed pairwise subtotal. Analyzed writer counts and pairwise totals are transcribed from Supplement Table S1; the combined-AI count uses the printed total for the two AI arms, without addition or subtraction. The supplement prints regression SEs and Human-only intercept estimates with their SEs. Neither document prints rating-level or participant-level SDs for this outcome or numerical confidence-interval endpoints. The reported b is an unstandardized coefficient. The percentage is transcribed in its printed units; no effect or arm mean is derived. The rating code is used because the schema has no evaluator category; it does not assert that the paper treated every rating as independent. The unadjusted model contains only assigned-condition indicators and a constant, so its printed Constant and parenthesized SE are recorded as the Human-only mean and its model-based SE. Treatment means are not computed from the constant and coefficient. Existing main-text p-values are retained. For otherwise missing p-values, significance symbols supply the printed upper bound and an unmarked coefficient leaves p_value null. The multi-regressor F-Stat is an omnibus model test and is not entered as a test of either individual AI-arm contrast. Supplement Table S3 confirms the significant one-idea result printed on main PDF p. 3; the wording on main PDF p. 2 emphasizing statistically significant gains only in the five-idea arm remains inconsistent.

estimates.notes: Each writer contributes one story; the paper specifies OLS with robust SEs for writer-study outcomes (PDF p. 8), so se_basis is participant. n_units is the printed total of stories in the full three-arm analysis, not a printed pairwise subtotal. Analyzed writer counts and pairwise totals are transcribed from Supplement Table S1; the combined-AI count uses the printed total for the two AI arms, without addition or subtraction. The supplement supplies the robust regression SE and the Human-only intercept SE; numerical confidence-interval endpoints and AI-arm SDs are not printed. This outcome concerns resemblance to an AI idea, not diversity across different people, and is coded with_ai/other. The screening form moved former outcome S1-O10 into its notes solely because of its outcome cap; the extraction specification has no such cap, so both contrasts are retained with form_outcome_id null. Supplement Section 3 specifies randomly sampling an AI idea generated for the same story topic, corroborating main PDF p. 5 and clarifying the conflicting same-condition wording on main PDF p. 8. Treatment means are not derived by adding coefficients to the printed control mean. The unadjusted model contains only assigned-condition indicators and a constant, so its printed Constant and parenthesized SE are recorded as the Human-only mean and its model-based SE. Treatment means are not computed from the constant and coefficient. Existing main-text p-values are retained. For otherwise missing p-values, significance symbols supply the printed upper bound and an unmarked coefficient leaves p_value null. The multi-regressor F-Stat is an omnibus model test and is not entered as a test of either individual AI-arm contrast. The Human-only SD comes from the full Human group in Table S12; statistics for the self-selected AI-use groups are not substituted for randomized AI arms. Table S11 prints the coefficient as 4.105, while the main text prints 4.11; the main-text value is retained, with the supplement precision documented here. Neither similarity outcome is listed in the complete preregistration, so preregistered_primary is no.

Human-only and pairwise participant totals are not printed and are not obtained by subtraction or addition. No rating-level or participant-level outcome SD, numerical SE, or numerical confidence interval is printed in the available PDF. This full-sample component contrast is displayed in Fig. 2A, but its coefficient, p-value, interval endpoints, and arm summaries are not numerically printed in the available text. No number is estimated from the figure. The composite index is preregistered; primary status of the individual item is not stated. Exact question wording is referred to unavailable supplementary sections S7 and S8. The rating code is used because the schema has no evaluator category; it does not assert that the paper treated every rating as independent.
